notes.q01: The reply denies that innate means always present, which answers D's dreamless-sleep argument directly.
notes.q02: The reply rejects reading idea as corporeal image, which is the premise of C's Angel/God objection.
notes.q03: A says only some bodies are divisible, which removes the contrast the conclusion needs; B says every body is divisible.
notes.q04: D picks up 'inconceivable' and talks about conceiving one's own non-existence, both from the objection.
notes.q05: B gives an a fortiori ground (civil power depends on grace less); A's 'different matters' gives no support.
notes.q06: The reply about dreaming of past events and the Atheist's certainty answers C point for point.
notes.q07: A jumps to 'every principle about heat and cold' being false; B concludes only that the stated principle is false.
notes.q08: The reply rebuts the claim that space has parts, which is the closing premise of A.
notes.q09: A's premise covers only 'some goods' but the conclusion is about 'all'; B's premise covers all goods.
notes.q10: B says the causes may be wholly unlike, which contradicts its own conclusion; A infers like causes from like effects.
notes.q11: B states there is one simple uniform sensation, which supports the identity; A's growing intensity does not.
notes.q12: The reply offers to give back the 'lost island', so it answers D's island objection.
notes.q13: A replies directly to the claim that reasoning only strings names together and so that mind is motion.
notes.q14: B's premise that instantaneous motion is impossible completes the reductio; A says it is not impossible.
notes.q15: A says some unperceiving things can feel pain, which undercuts its conclusion; B has the needed universal premise.
notes.q16: The premise is about divine law only; B over-extends the conclusion to human law.
notes.q17: A attacks the relational view of space and time as an order of coexistences and successions, which is the objection's position.
notes.q18: A needs God to be indefensible if the ideas came from non-bodies for the conclusion to follow; B grants the opposite.
notes.q19: B answers the claim that God cannot be conceived from any like reality by ascending from lesser goods to greater.
notes.q20: A explicitly addresses the painter analogy being unnecessary.
